主要内容: Target reported its first quarter 2019 earnings, which exceeded analysts' expectations. The company's adjusted earnings per share reached $1.53, surpassing the expected $1.43. Revenues totaled $17.63 billion, beating the forecast of $17.52 billion. Same-store sales increased by 4.8%, outperforming the expected 4.2% growth. Target's digital sales surged 42%, with online transactions now accounting for 7.1% of total transactions, up from 5.2% a year ago. CEO Brian Cornell stated that Target is well-positioned to deliver strong financial performance in 2019 and beyond. The company also maintained its full-year outlook despite the looming threat of 25% tariffs on apparel and footwear from China. Target shares jumped nearly 10% following the report, contrasting with the disappointing results of other department store chains earlier in the week. Target reported its first quarter 2019 earnings, highlighting its efforts to enhance customer relevance through new product lines and strategic collaborations. The company launched intimates and sleepwear brands Auden, Stars Above, and Colsie, which were well received. Target also introduced an environmentally friendly cleaning-products brand called Everspring. The company's Chief Marketing Officer, Mark Tritton, emphasized that integrating merchandising efforts with other business initiatives makes Target more relevant to customers. Morgan Stanley upgraded Target shares, calling it a "survivor" in retail, and noted that the company is beyond its "peak margin pain." Target's gross-margin rate declined slightly due to increased supply-chain and digital-fulfillment costs. The company also launched a limited-edition line with Vineyard Vines, which was highly successful. Target shares are up about 8.8% for the year, with a market cap of approximately $39.8 billion.
